vocabulary.definition: a virtual reality space where users can interact with a computer-generated environment and other users
vocabulary.example: People will spend more time in the metaverse, living and working in virtual worlds.

vocabulary.definition: deeply engaging or absorbing; surrounding the user's senses and making them feel involved
vocabulary.example: The virtual reality experience was so immersive that it felt like being in a different world.

vocabulary.definition: having doubts or reservations about something; being skeptical
vocabulary.example: Doctor Nicola Millard is sceptical about the practicality of virtual reality technology.

vocabulary.definition: difficult to move or handle due to size, weight, or complexity
vocabulary.example: The VR headset was so unwieldy that it made Nicola feel uncomfortable.

vocabulary.definition: a blend of physical and digital elements, combining features of both worlds
vocabulary.example: Emma Ridderstad envisions a phygital future where digital and physical objects interact seamlessly.

vocabulary.definition: technology that overlays digital information onto the physical world, enhancing the user's perception of reality
vocabulary.example: With augmented reality glasses, users can see virtual images superimposed onto their real surroundings.
